# The complete transitive closure of requirements.txt, captured from a working environment.
# requirements.txt is the human-authored list of what this app directly needs; this file is
# every package that actually ends up installed, pinned exactly.
#
# Use it to reproduce a build (`pip install -r requirements.lock.txt`) and so vulnerability
# scanners can see the whole dependency tree rather than just the top level — most findings
# live in transitive packages that never appear in requirements.txt.
#
# `--all` is deliberate: plain `pip freeze` omits pip/setuptools/wheel, and setuptools is
# pinned for a security reason (see requirements.txt), so leaving it out would drop that pin
# silently. `pip` itself is excluded — pinning the installer that is mid-install is a good
# way to have a bad afternoon.
#
# Regenerate after changing any pin:
#   python -m pip freeze --all --exclude-editable > requirements.lock.txt   (then drop pip==)
#
